tZh: OpenAI 解雇三名安全研究员
sEn: OpenAI's opaque firing of three safety researchers has created a chilling effect on safety advocacy and damaged trust, requiring costly, credible signals that safety advocacy is welcome.
sZh: OpenAI 解雇三名安全研究员且缺乏公开解释，对安全倡导造成寒蝉效应并损害信任，需以高成本的可信信号表明安全倡导不会危及员工职位。
absEn: The article examines OpenAI's firing of three safety researchers—Tomek Korbak, Mikita Balesni, and Jasmine Wang—and the ensuing controversy over whether they were dismissed for safety advocacy or for legitimate breaches of trust. It argues that the firings, whatever the true cause, were an expensive and damaging action: the employees were highly valuable, and the lack of public explanation has created a chilling effect on safety advocacy both inside OpenAI and across the broader AI safety ecosystem. The author believes OpenAI's claim that the real reasons were not those named by the employees, but notes that the company's opaque process and its history of similar cases make it impossible to rule out pretextual firing. The conclusion is that OpenAI must send costly, credible signals that safety advocacy is welcomed and will not cost employees their jobs, or the damage to trust and to the safety ecosystem will persist.
absZh: 本文审视了 OpenAI 解雇三名安全研究员——Tomek Korbak、Mikita Balesni 和 Jasmine Wang——一事，以及随之而来的争议：他们究竟是因为倡导安全而被解雇，还是因为确实违反了信任。文章认为，无论真实原因为何，此次解雇都是一次代价高昂且具有破坏性的行动：这些员工极具价值，而缺乏公开解释已在 OpenAI 内部及更广泛的 AI 安全生态系统中对安全倡导造成了寒蝉效应。作者相信 OpenAI 所称的真实原因并非员工所指的那些，但也指出，该公司不透明的流程及其类似案例的历史，使得无法排除借故解雇的可能性。结论是，OpenAI 必须发出代价高昂且可信的信号，表明安全倡导受到欢迎且不会让员工丢掉工作，否则对信任和安全生态系统的损害将持续存在。

contrib.en: Argues the firing of three safety researchers was costly and damaging, creating a chilling effect on safety advocacy.
contrib.zh: 认为解雇三名安全研究员代价高昂且具破坏性，对安全倡导产生了寒蝉效应。

contrib.en: Contends OpenAI's opaque process and history of similar cases make pretextual firing impossible to rule out.
contrib.zh: 主张 OpenAI 不透明的流程和类似案例的历史使得无法排除借口解雇的可能性。

contrib.en: Highlights the employees' parting recommendations on chain-of-thought monitoring and embedded evaluators.
contrib.zh: 强调员工关于思维链监控和嵌入式评估器的离职建议。

contrib.en: Calls for costly, credible signals that safety advocacy is welcomed and will not cost jobs.
contrib.zh: 呼吁发出代价高昂、可信的信号，表明安全倡导受到欢迎且不会危及工作。

contrib.en: Notes the public silence from OpenAI staff and the broader chilling effect across the AI safety ecosystem.
contrib.zh: 指出 OpenAI 员工的公开沉默以及整个 AI 安全生态系统中更广泛的寒蝉效应。

limits.en: Lacks direct evidence; relies on public statements and speculation about internal reasons.
limits.zh: 缺乏直接证据；依赖公开声明和对内部原因的推测。

limits.en: Author's belief that firings were not for safety advocacy is asserted without proof.
limits.zh: 作者关于解雇并非因安全倡导的信念缺乏证据支持。

limits.en: Does not consider that legal or confidentiality constraints may prevent OpenAI from sharing details.
limits.zh: 未考虑法律或保密限制可能阻止 OpenAI 分享细节。

limits.en: Assumes the employees' accounts are sincere, though acknowledges they may withhold core reasons.
limits.zh: 假设员工的陈述是真诚的，尽管承认他们可能隐瞒核心原因。

limits.en: Focuses on a single incident; broader systemic issues in AI safety governance are not analyzed.
limits.zh: 聚焦于单一事件；未分析 AI 安全治理中更广泛的系统性问题。

paras.en: 6.   OpenAI Firing These Employees for Safety Advocacy Would Be Deeply Stupid.
paras.zh: 6.   OpenAI 因员工倡导安全而解雇他们将是极其愚蠢的。

paras.en: 14.   No One Is Buying OpenAI's Non-Explanations.
paras.zh: 14.   没有人会相信 OpenAI 那些毫无解释力的说辞。

paras.en: All three had expressed alarm recently on Twitter:
paras.zh: 这三人最近都在 Twitter 上表达了警觉：

paras.en: These are legit researchers who were at the center of safety efforts. OpenAI firing them is a tragedy, whether or not OpenAI was justified in firing them, or was effectively forced to do so. Tomek Korbak in particular had also been one of the louder OpenAI voices of concern about recent alignment difficulties with Astra and its lack of monitorability.
paras.zh: 这些都是身处安全努力核心的正当研究者。OpenAI 解雇他们是一场悲剧，无论 OpenAI 解雇他们是否正当，还是实际上是被迫这样做。尤其是 Tomek Korbak，他也曾是 OpenAI 内部对近期 Astra 对齐困难及其缺乏可监控性表达担忧的更大声的声音之一。

paras.en: We were given an official statement, but it did not say much.
paras.zh: 我们收到了一份官方声明，但其中并未透露多少信息。

paras.en: OpenAI also said that the misconduct went past sharing information with an outside analysis firm, and that no one was fired for raising safety concerns. They declined at the time to name the fired employees.
paras.zh: OpenAI 还表示，不当行为不仅限于与外部分析公司分享信息，且没有人因提出安全担忧而被解雇。他们当时拒绝透露被解雇员工的姓名。

paras.en: We don’t know, from that description, where this lands from ‘fired the whistleblowers on a pretext’ to ‘holy hell, you cannot do that, yes we actually have to fire you.’ There is mishandling information, and then there is mishandling information.
paras.zh: 根据这一描述，我们无法确定此事究竟属于‘以借口解雇举报人’还是‘天哪，你不能这样做，是的，我们确实必须解雇你’的范畴。信息处理不当也有程度之分。

paras.en: We still don’t have a public explanation beyond OpenAI’s initial statement. There are many reasons that could be the case. Some are benign. Others are not.
paras.zh: 除了 OpenAI 的初步声明，我们仍然没有公开的解释。造成这种情况的原因有很多。有些是善意的，有些则不是。

paras.en: It was very reasonable for many to assume, until proven otherwise—given the track record of OpenAI and the lack of further explanation—that it was the first one.
paras.zh: 鉴于 OpenAI 的过往记录以及缺乏进一步解释，许多人在被证明并非如此之前，有理由认为这是第一种情况。

paras.en: Remember that Leopold Aschenbrenner credibly claims he was fired from OpenAI on a pretext for taking security concerns to the board, and there are many other cases that at least rhyme with the current one.
paras.zh: 请记住，Leopold Aschenbrenner 可信地声称，他因将安全方面的担忧提交给董事会而被 OpenAI 以借口解雇，还有许多其他案例至少与当前这一案例如出一辙。

paras.en: The incident with Leopold might be impacting this one. Leopold says he was told, very explicitly, the action that got him fired. That made OpenAI look worse, not better.
paras.zh: Leopold 的事件可能正在影响这一事件。Leopold 说，他被告知了导致他被解雇的具体行为，而且说得非常明确。这让 OpenAI 显得更糟，而不是更好。

paras.en: We learned from a WSJ report that the three fired OpenAI employees were calling for additional safety measures around preserving chain-of-thought monitoring, and that they (as one would expect) take issue with OpenAI's characterization of the firings:
paras.zh: 我们从《华尔街日报》的报道中了解到，被解雇的三名 OpenAI 员工呼吁在保留思维链监控方面采取额外的安全措施，并且他们（如人们所料）对 OpenAI 对解雇事件的描述提出异议：

paras.en: Here are their parting recommendations to OpenAI:
paras.zh: 以下是他们给 OpenAI 的临别建议：

paras.en: They go into more detail in the full letter. Everyone I respect on these matters fully agrees with these recommendations.
paras.zh: 他们在完整信函中提供了更多细节。我在这方面尊重的所有人都完全同意这些建议。

paras.en: So does OpenAI, or at least they are strongly saying that they agree.
paras.zh: OpenAI 也是如此，或者至少他们强烈表示同意。

paras.en: Given the decision to make only modest requests of OpenAI, the prescriptive part is going about as well as one could hope.
paras.zh: 鉴于只对 OpenAI 提出适度要求的决定，规范部分进展得如人所愿。

paras.en: The problem is that OpenAI would express strong support for all three of these proposals, even if they did not strongly support these proposals. I am happy with their statements on this matter that I have seen.
paras.zh: 问题在于，即便 OpenAI 并不强烈支持这三项提议，它也会对这三项提议都表达强烈支持。对于我目前看到的他们就此事发表的声明，我感到满意。

paras.en: There was no world where OpenAI was going to get up and say they do not support an open and transparent culture of dialogue, or that they no longer care about monitorability, or that they are abandoning their public commitments on embedded evaluators.
paras.zh: OpenAI 绝不可能站出来说他们不支持开放透明的对话文化，或者说他们不再关心可监控性，又或者他们正在放弃关于嵌入式评估者的公开承诺。

paras.en: The only way to affirm an open and transparent culture of dialogue, and okay with full collaboration with outsiders and auditors and evaluators on safety issues, is to send costly or otherwise credible signals that you are truly okay with that, and not only will it not get you fired it will be at worst neutral for your career.
paras.zh: 要肯定开放透明的对话文化，并表明完全愿意与外部人员、审计员和评估者在安全问题上充分合作，唯一的方法就是发出代价高昂或其他可信的信号，表明你真心支持这一点，而且这不仅不会让你被解雇，最坏情况下对你的职业生涯也是中性的。

paras.en: That is not easy. OpenAI has done a lot of good work here over time exactly by having a bunch of people, including Roon, post a lot of things. We need a lot of things, but one of them is that we need more questionable posting, stat.
paras.zh: 这并不容易。OpenAI 长期以来在这方面做了很多出色的工作，正是通过让包括 Roon 在内的许多人发布大量内容。我们需要很多东西，但其中之一就是我们需要更多有问题的帖子，立刻马上。

paras.en: One of the letter’s asks is highly relevant here:
paras.zh: 信中的一项要求与此高度相关：

paras.en: Those rules being clear and good will be a key early test.
paras.zh: 这些规则是否清晰且良好，将是一个关键的早期考验。

paras.en: If OpenAI wants to undo the damage and chilling effect, including at other labs, they have to convince their employees, and ideally everyone, that safety advocacy, both internal and external, had nothing to do with why these three employees were fired.
paras.zh: 如果 OpenAI 想要消除损害和寒蝉效应（包括在其他实验室），他们必须说服自己的员工，最好说服所有人，安全倡导——无论是内部还是外部——与这三名员工被解雇的原因无关。

paras.en: OpenAI must give confidence that trust was lost for other good reasons, and that such fierce advocacy was and continues to be welcomed and celebrated. Or they’ll have to prove that, over time, in other ways.
paras.zh: OpenAI 必须让人相信，信任是因其他正当理由而失去的，并且这种激烈的倡导过去和现在都受到欢迎和赞扬。否则，他们就必须通过其他方式，随着时间的推移来证明这一点。

paras.en: I respect that, if OpenAI did have good reasons, there are legal and ethical and also practical reasons why it is difficult for OpenAI to share those reasons even in the best of situations, and this is not the best of situations. It is what it is. Choices are made.
paras.zh: 我尊重这一点：如果 OpenAI 确实有正当理由，那么即使在最好的情况下，法律、道德以及实际方面的原因也会让 OpenAI 难以分享这些理由，而目前并非最好的情况。事情就是这样。选择已经做出。

full.sec: OpenAI Firing These Employees For Safety Advocacy Would Be Deeply Stupid
full.secZh: OpenAI 因安全倡导解雇员工将极为愚蠢

paras.en: I don’t know the real reason these three employees were fired.
paras.zh: 我不知道这三名员工被解雇的真正原因。

paras.en: Even the employees don’t fully know. They can guess, but the process is opaque. There are many reasons, good and bad, why the reason you are given may not be the real one, or the central one, or the whole story.
paras.zh: 甚至员工自己也不完全清楚。他们可以猜测，但过程是不透明的。有很多原因，好的和坏的，为什么给你的理由可能不是真实的，或者不是核心的，或者不是全部。

paras.en: What I do know, and what is being neglected in discussions over these events, is that ‘these three high level and highly valuable OpenAI safety researchers were fired for their safety advocacy’ would be deeply, deeply stupid.
paras.zh: 我所知道的是，并且在关于这些事件的讨论中被忽视的是，“这三名高级且极具价值的 OpenAI 安全研究员因他们的安全倡导而被解雇”将是极其、极其愚蠢的。

paras.en: These were extremely valuable employees, whose loss will hurt. If you fire them without good cause, the world is going to notice this, and it is going to be an extremely bad look, and have a chilling effect and damage the safety ecosystem, and potentially cost you other current and potential employees.
paras.zh: 这些是极其宝贵的员工，他们的离去将造成伤害。如果你没有正当理由解雇他们，世界会注意到这一点，这将是一个极其糟糕的形象，并产生寒蝉效应，损害安全生态系统，并可能让你失去其他现任和潜在员工。

paras.en: This was an expensive action to take even if the three employees had gone quietly. And if you fire them on pretexts, it is going to be even more expensive.
paras.zh: 即使这三名员工安静地离开，这也是一个代价高昂的行动。而如果你以借口解雇他们，代价将更加高昂。

paras.en: Some will say that the chilling effect on safety advocacy and cooperation was the point, to cripple such efforts and avoid future exposure of future problems. I don’t buy that, and if it was true there were vastly better ways to go about getting the part of this that OpenAI finds valuable.
paras.zh: 有人会说，对安全倡导与合作的寒蝉效应正是目的所在，旨在削弱此类努力并避免未来问题被曝光。我不认同这种说法；如果真是如此，原本有更好的办法来获取 OpenAI 认为有价值的部分。

paras.en: The story that this was based centrally on any form of public communications or internal championing of various safety measures, and that everything else is pure pretext, never made sense to me.
paras.zh: 那种认为此事主要基于任何形式的公开沟通或内部对各项安全措施的倡导，而其他一切纯属借口的说法，我从未觉得合理。

paras.en: We also know that the reasons in the letter were not the central reason, because that is contradicted by OpenAI Newsroom’s Tweet (reproduced in full later) referring to a breach of trust, combined with the reasons otherwise looking like pretexts. Something happened, that we do not know about.
paras.zh: 我们也知道，信中的理由并非核心原因，因为这与 OpenAI Newsroom 的推文（稍后全文转载）提到的信任破裂相矛盾，而且这些理由看起来像是借口。发生了某些我们不知道的事情。

paras.en: That still leaves the central question unanswered. Why were they fired?
paras.zh: 这仍然留下核心问题未答：他们为什么被解雇？

paras.en: The three employees have now come out, in the letter and on Twitter, to say that they have not done anything they feel merits this action, and that if OpenAI has particular accusations against them they would very much like to know what those are.
paras.zh: 这三名员工现在通过公开信和 Twitter 发声，表示他们并未做过任何自认为应受此处理的事情，并且如果 OpenAI 对他们有具体指控，他们非常想知道这些指控是什么。

paras.en: They start off denying they were the source for the architectural leak to The Information. They also disavow another rumor about a shared board-level memo, and say they did not tell the media that they were fired. These are not accusations that have been officially made by OpenAI. I have seen nothing concrete about the origin of those rumors, other than Jasmine's claims about this.
paras.zh: 他们首先否认自己是向 The Information 泄露架构信息的消息源。他们还否认了另一则关于共享董事会备忘录的传言，并表示他们没有告诉媒体自己被解雇。这些都不是 OpenAI 官方提出的指控。除了 Jasmine 对此的说法外，我没有看到任何关于这些传言来源的具体证据。

paras.en: There is then a different description for each of them, both within the letter and from their Tweets, because each of them says they were given a different explanation.
paras.zh: 随后，公开信和他们的推文中对每个人的描述各不相同，因为他们每个人都表示自己得到了不同的解释。

paras.en: First off, there's Tomek Korbak. He was the METR point of contact for their investigation.
paras.zh: 首先是 Tomek Korbak。他是 METR 调查的对接联系人。

paras.en: Tomek Korbak is famously the one who Tweeted:
paras.zh: Tomek Korbak 正是那位发推文的人，这一点广为人知：

paras.en: He says he was told he was fired because of the way he communicated with METR, with no further explanations given.
paras.zh: 他说，他被告知自己之所以被解雇，是因为他与 METR 沟通的方式，除此之外没有给出任何进一步解释。

paras.en: Certainly there are 'ways of communicating with METR' that force one to be fired, for example (this is purely me guessing based on public info) sharing sufficiently valuable trade secrets, or sending sufficiently sensitive information through insecure or inappropriate channels, especially with a pattern of such behavior. It would take quite a lot to justify a firing over this, but it is possible.
paras.zh: 当然，确实存在一些“与 METR 沟通的方式”会迫使人被解雇，例如（这纯粹是我基于公开信息的猜测）分享了足够有价值的商业机密，或通过不安全或不恰当的渠道发送了足够敏感的信息，尤其是存在此类行为的模式。要以此为由解雇一个人，需要相当充分的理由，但这是可能的。

paras.en: Perhaps Korbak is wrong about how much he was told, or this is a very clear case of 'oh he damn well knows what he did.' Or perhaps there is a sincere disagreement over the severity of whatever happened. We cannot be sure.
paras.zh: 也许 Korbak 对自己被告知了多少内容存在误解，或者这是一个非常明确的“他明明很清楚自己做了什么”的情形。又或者，双方对所发生之事的严重程度存在真诚的分歧。我们无法确定。

paras.en: But even if OpenAI is entirely both justified and honest here, and Korbak communicated with METR in ways so unacceptable that trust was lost and he therefore had to be fired?
paras.zh: 但即便 OpenAI 在此完全既有正当理由又诚实，且 Korbak 与 METR 的沟通方式如此不可接受，以至于信任丧失、他因此不得不被解雇，那又如何？

paras.en: The way this was communicated, both to Korbak and to the world, including in response to Korbak's claims, combined with the circumstances, is a huge problem.
paras.zh: 这件事的传达方式——无论是对 Korbak 还是对全世界，包括对 Korbak 说法的回应——再加上当时的具体情况，是一个巨大的问题。

paras.en: I believe that Korbak believes this. Otherwise he is outright lying, and his actions would otherwise not make sense.
paras.zh: 我相信 Korbak 相信这一点。否则他就是在公然撒谎，而他的行为否则就说不通了。

paras.en: I believe that Mikita believes the firing was pretextual. The only alternative, given his description, is that Mikita is lying.
paras.zh: 我认为 Mikita 相信这次解雇是借口。根据他的描述，唯一的另一种可能是 Mikita 在撒谎。

paras.en: Jasmine Wang also does not mince words, and lays out the choice: Either you trust her, or you trust OpenAI. She calls bullshit.
paras.zh: Jasmine Wang 同样直言不讳，并摆出了这个选择：要么你相信她，要么你相信 OpenAI。她直言这是胡扯。

paras.en: I believe that Jasmine Wang, too, believes what she is saying. She issues the challenge:
paras.zh: 我相信 Jasmine Wang 也相信自己所说的话。她提出了这一挑战：

paras.en: Jasmine Wang says she had extended unnecessary access to the emails of an executive.
paras.zh: Jasmine Wang 表示，她曾获得对一位高管电子邮件的、超出必要范围的访问权限。

paras.en: Is it just me, or is that a really terrible security failure for a company at the level of OpenAI? This is not the main thing, but how is this not truly horrible operational security?
paras.zh: 是我多心了吗，还是说对于一家 OpenAI 这种级别的公司而言，这确实是一次极其严重的安全失误？这不是重点，但这怎么能不算真正糟糕的运营安全？

paras.en: It would be bad enough to have the executive emails at all, well after she had need for them and requested to no longer have access, but to have them intertwined with her own, a detail it seems absurd to make up? What the hell?
paras.zh: 在她早已不再需要这些邮件、并已请求撤销访问权限之后，仍然持有这些高管邮件就已经够糟了；但这些邮件竟与她的个人邮件混在一起——这种细节编造出来似乎都显得荒谬？这到底是怎么回事？

paras.en: It seems plausible to fire someone over that fact, distinct from what was or wasn't done with that access. That person should presumably not be Jasmine Wang.
paras.zh: 仅凭这一事实就解雇某人似乎也说得通，这与利用该访问权限做了什么或没做什么是两回事。但那个人想必不应该是 Jasmine Wang。

paras.en: This was OpenAI's official response to the three researchers. **Bold mine.**
paras.zh: 这是 OpenAI 对三位研究者的官方回应。**加粗为笔者所加。**

paras.en: There are two key implied claims here, although they are not logically forced.
paras.zh: 这里有两个关键的隐含主张，尽管它们在逻辑上并非必然成立。

paras.en: 1. The underlying justification relied on key events not named by the employees.
paras.zh: 1. 其背后的理由依赖于员工并未点名的关键事件。

paras.en: 2. A key underlying justification is this 'significant breach of trust,' whatever that is.
paras.zh: 2. 一个关键的底层理由便是这种“重大的信任破裂”，无论它具体指什么。

paras.en: I believe OpenAI on both counts. Nothing else makes sense.
paras.zh: 在这两点上我都相信 OpenAI。否则一切就说不通了。

paras.en: It was never likely that there were three top safety researchers who centrally broke trust in three distinct ways. Much more likely is one particular cause, and one investigation into one central cause, whatever it was.
paras.zh: 三名顶尖安全研究员以三种截然不同的方式在核心层面破坏信任，这从来都不太可能。更可能的是存在某一个特定原因，以及针对某一个核心原因的一次调查，无论它是什么。

paras.en: That does not mean that the researchers did anything wrong, or that what they did wrong rose to the level of 'you need to be fired.' It does mean that somehow things escalated to the point where trust had broken down, no matter who was at fault.
paras.zh: 这并不意味着研究人员做错了什么，或者他们的错误达到了‘你该被解雇’的程度。这确实意味着，不知何故事情升级到了信任破裂的地步，无论是谁的错。

paras.en: 1. OpenAI's core reasons (good or bad, true or false) went unshared.
paras.zh: 1. OpenAI 的核心原因（无论好坏，真假）未被分享。

paras.en: 2. The employees were told the core reasons, and are withholding that.
paras.zh: 2. 员工被告知了核心原因，但对此保密。

paras.en: Trust is not optional. If it is irrevocably broken, you don't have a choice, no matter what caused that break in the first place. But nothing we know about seems like it should rise to a level that should irrevocably break trust.
paras.zh: 信任不是可选项。如果信任被不可挽回地破坏，无论最初是什么导致了破裂，你都没有选择。但据我们所知，似乎没有什么应该达到不可挽回地破坏信任的程度。

paras.en: OpenAI also says that they do not anticipate that further information exchange would lead to a resolution. I believe them. OpenAI has an explicit request from the employees to share more information, but that does not make this wise. Sometimes you are doing your best and yet saying more things would only make things worse.
paras.zh: OpenAI 还表示，他们预计进一步的信息交流不会导致解决方案。我相信他们。OpenAI 有员工明确要求分享更多信息，但这并不使这样做明智。有时你尽了最大努力，但说更多的话只会让事情更糟。

paras.en: That does not get OpenAI out of the consequences of being this avoidant.
paras.zh: 这并不能让 OpenAI 摆脱如此回避所带来的后果。

paras.en: The term appears both in the letter and the response.
paras.zh: 该词在信件和回应中均有出现。

paras.en: OpenAI Newsroom says in its response: “We will continue to be extremely forgiving of our team making good-faith mistakes.”
paras.zh: OpenAI Newsroom 在其回应中表示：“对于团队出于善意所犯的错误，我们将继续保持极度宽容。”

paras.en: The employee letter says of Mikita: “He acted throughout in good faith and within the company’s norms as they stood at the time.”
paras.zh: 员工信件在谈及 Mikita 时写道：“他自始至终都出于善意行事，并且符合公司当时的规范。”

paras.en: Kobeck and Wang also tell stories that either are themselves told in bad faith, or clearly indicate their actions at OpenAI were in good faith.
paras.zh: Kobeck 和 Wang 所讲述的故事，要么本身是出于恶意讲述的，要么清楚地表明他们在 OpenAI 的行为是出于善意的。

full.sec: No One Is Buying OpenAI’s Non-Explanations
full.secZh: 无人买账：OpenAI 的非解释

paras.en: Alas, in order to use terms like 'a significant breach of trust' and be trusted, you need to have not had many 'significant breaches of trust' in your company's past.
paras.zh: 唉，要想使用‘严重违背信任’这样的说法并取信于人，你的公司过去就不能有太多‘严重违背信任’的记录。

paras.en: At minimum, even before we got the response from the fired employees, we could all agree with Joshua Achiam that, barring unexpected new information, this is a terrible look from OpenAI, as well as a large practical loss. Not that there is a great time to fire such people, but this was an extremely poor time.
paras.zh: 至少，在我们收到被解雇员工的回应之前，我们都可以同意 Joshua Achiam 的观点：除非出现意外的新信息，否则这对 OpenAI 来说非常难看，也是一个巨大的实际损失。并不是说解雇这些人有什么好时机，但这是一个极其糟糕的时机。

paras.en: In the wake of the additional information, things look worse.
paras.zh: 随着更多信息的披露，情况看起来更糟了。

paras.en: I don't think this is strictly required, if there were sufficient communication breakdowns, depending on how you view incomplete explanations for being fired.
paras.zh: 我不认为这是严格必需的，如果存在足够的沟通障碍，这取决于你如何看待被解雇的不完整解释。

paras.en: The obvious alternative hypothesis is 'disgruntled employees mad over being fired' but Kelsey Piper says she knows two of the three and this is not like that:
paras.zh: 显而易见的替代假设是‘心怀不满的员工因被解雇而愤怒’，但 Kelsey Piper 说她认识三人中的两人，情况并非如此：

paras.en: There are many calling these three whistleblowers. We do not know that this is true, given I do not hear any blown whistles or claims to having blown one? But certainly the pattern suggests a concern.
paras.zh: 许多人称这三人为吹哨人。鉴于我并未听到任何哨声，也没有听到任何人声称自己吹过哨，我们无从得知这是否属实？但这一模式无疑暗示着某种隐忧。

full.sec: The Dog Did Nothing in the Nighttime

paras.en: No members of technical staff, or executives, have spoken about this in public.
paras.zh: 没有任何技术团队成员或高管公开谈论过此事。

paras.en: Far more troubling, in response to an event that has a potential chilling effect, there are exceptions but almost none of the many people I keep tabs on from OpenAI other than Dean Ball are saying anything on Twitter at all, about almost any subject. Of the statements I have seen, none are at all controversial or frisky.
paras.zh: 更令人不安的是，面对一个可能产生寒蝉效应的事件，除 Dean Ball 之外，我持续关注的许多 OpenAI 人士几乎无人在 Twitter 上就几乎任何话题发声——当然也有例外。在我所见过的表态中，没有一条有任何争议性或冒进之处。

paras.en: I do not at all blame the OpenAI employees for this. The situation is complicated, with much we do not know. Public silence is a highly reasonable move while things play out internally. The silence is still deafening.
paras.zh: 我完全不怪 OpenAI 的员工。情况很复杂，有很多我们不知道的事。在事情于内部推进期间，公开保持沉默是非常合理的做法。但这沉默依然震耳欲聋。

full.sec: Another Theory (That I Do Not Agree With)
full.secZh: 另一种理论（我并不赞同）

paras.en: Opinions I disagree with but that are out there: There are even those, like Arjun Panickssery and charding, who think that the reported reasons looking like obvious pretexts is a feature rather than a bug. Under this theory, if you gave a plausible pretext, people might believe it, and that would defeat the purpose of creating a chilling effect.
paras.zh: 我并不同意的观点，但确实存在：甚至有人，比如 Arjun Panickssery 和 charding，认为所报告的理由看起来像明显的借口，这是一种特性而非缺陷。在这种理论下，如果你给出一个看似合理的借口，人们可能会相信它，而这会破坏制造寒蝉效应的目的。

full.sec: The Reactions Are Not a Surprise Given the Actions
full.secZh: 鉴于所采取的行动，这些反应并不令人意外

paras.en: Again, these reactions should not come as a surprise to anyone involved. This was always going to look pretty damn messed up. If OpenAI had a way to make it look not pretty damn messed up, that it was able to share, we would know about it by now.
paras.zh: 再次强调，这些反应对任何相关方来说都不应感到意外。这件事看起来一直都会显得相当糟糕。如果 OpenAI 有办法让它看起来不那么糟糕，并且能够分享出来，我们早就应该知道了。

paras.en: I do not believe the fired employees are lying to us. I see no reason for them to be doing that, and if they are lying about the exit meetings then OpenAI has the ability to contradict this. If that is correct it means that OpenAI at minimum massively dropped the ball on its communications, both to the employees and to the public, even if we are otherwise maximally charitable. Allowing such obviously pretextual explanations to become the story of what the employees were told is just so, so bad on its own, no matter the underlying facts.
paras.zh: 我不认为被解雇的员工在欺骗我们。我看不出他们有什么理由这样做，而且如果他们在离职会议的事情上撒谎，OpenAI 有能力反驳这一点。如果这是正确的，那就意味着 OpenAI 至少在沟通上严重失职，无论是对员工还是对公众，即使我们在其他方面给予最大限度的宽容。允许这种明显是借口的解释成为员工被告知内容的说法，这本身就非常非常糟糕，无论背后的事实如何。

full.sec: This Is Terrible But Not Maximally Terrible
full.secZh: 这很糟糕，但并非最糟糕

paras.en: I do think many are jumping to a ‘maximally messed up’ interpretation that I find unlikely to be true, because of the incentives involved.
paras.zh: 我确实认为许多人都跳到了“最混乱”的解释上，而我觉得这不太可能为真，因为其中涉及激励因素。

paras.en: Here are some things that make the situation less than maximally terrible:
paras.zh: 以下是一些让情况不至于最糟糕的因素：

paras.en: 1. I believe that OpenAI did NOT fire these employees due to their publicly or internally expressed concerns about safety.
paras.zh: 1. 我相信 OpenAI 解雇这些员工并非因为他们公开或内部表达了对安全的担忧。

paras.en: 2. I believe that OpenAI did NOT fire these employees due to their advocacy of 3P commitments or third party auditors or embedded evaluators.
paras.zh: 2. 我相信 OpenAI 解雇这些员工并非因为他们倡导第三方承诺或第三方审计员或嵌入式评估员。

paras.en: 3. I believe that OpenAI did NOT fire these employees in order to create a chilling effect or reduce employee cooperation with third parties.
paras.zh: 3. 我相信 OpenAI 解雇这些员工并非为了制造寒蝉效应或减少员工与第三方的合作。

paras.en: That still leaves us without a good explanation, probably permanently, and with the three employees claiming, I believe sincerely, that they were fired for their safety advocacy. Given the long and positive track record of all three of them, this was at best a huge unforced error, even if OpenAI was for whatever reason backed into taking an L on this. And it goes into a long line of incidents that rhyme.
paras.zh: 这仍然让我们得不到一个好的解释，而且很可能永远得不到，同时那三名员工声称——我相信他们是真诚的——他们因倡导安全而被解雇。鉴于三人长期且良好的过往记录，这充其量是一个巨大的非受迫性失误，即便 OpenAI 出于某种原因被迫在这件事上认栽。而这又加入了长长一串彼此押韵的事件之列。
